method: Winners transcribed from the German Wikipedia historical winners list; expanded with English Wikipedia race and class tables. Class labels translated, names and marques normalised, repeated tables de-duplicated. Race average speeds are kept distinct from lap records. Gaps are not treated as zero results. This is a historical archive, not a live timing feed. Specific Formula TT race tables, class-winner lists and named-rider race records are used to reconcile known discrepancies. Co-riders in the 1975 and 1976 Production endurance races each receive a rider credit; motorcycle totals count once. Main statistics exclude Clubman’s and TTXGP unless extended scope is selected. Competition numbers are carried where a licensed 2024–2026 classification table prints them; a second, independent transcription of the same pages was checked against every winner and every recent classification, and the handful of winners it reads differently are listed in the data file, not applied.

landmarks.wp: en:List of named corners of the Snaefell Mountain Course

course.changes: Selected relation ways and named member nodes; coordinates projected for a local SVG display. Current mapped course, not historical geometry.

Mountain Course.note: The Snaefell Mountain Course, 37.73 miles from the Grandstand over the mountain and back, used from 1911 for every TT race that was not run on a short course.

St. John’s Short Course.note: The first course, 15.8 miles through St John’s, Ballacraine, Kirk Michael and Peel, used for the four TTs of 1907–1910.

Clypse Course.note: A 10.79-mile course from the Grandstand through Onchan and Creg-ny-Baa, used for the Lightweight, Ultra-Lightweight and Sidecar races of 1954–1959.

Billown Circuit.note: The 4.25-mile Castletown course of the Southern 100 and the Pre-TT Classic, used for support races.

harvest.title: Isle of Man TT rights-cleared data harvest
harvest.rightsPolicy: Include factual race data only from sources that expressly permit redistribution; exclude data under explicit reproduction prohibition or unclear terms.
harvest.attribution: The annual winners/status data and 2024–2026 results are adapted from Wikipedia pages licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. Attribute Wikipedia and the linked article sources, link the license, indicate changes, and distribute adaptations under CC BY-SA 4.0 or a compatible later version.
harvest.methodology: Data were transcribed from CC BY-SA 4.0 Wikipedia tables and normalized into fields. Sidecar entries keep both listed names together in riders. Machine strings are retained as published. Empty/placeholder standings were omitted. Race-status records distinguish cancellations/aborted races from race winners. Historical meeting cancellations are listed separately from cancelled race categories. The 2024 page provided 89 populated classifications across its 9 result headings (including additional finishers where listed); 2025 provided the top ten from nine completed races; 2026 provided five race tables. Source citations and row order were checked against page text. One 2026 race table conflicts with the article narrative and is explicitly flagged.

gaps: Full classified finishers and non-finishers are not comprehensively covered across historical years.
Lap-by-lap, stage/split, retirement, and incident details are not covered.
Annual winners are covered across the available 1907–2026 licensed index, but detailed finish order, timing, and speed remain absent for most years.
The official 1907-present database appears to be the most complete source, but its terms currently prevent redistribution without permission.
2026 Supersport Race 1 entry is disputed within its source article and should not be treated as confirmed.
